messages:
cheng: anyone seeing a weird queue in eu-west? GPUs ~20% used but token queue is 600+ and admission doesn't move
maria: yup, noticed it ~5m ago. autoscaler reports nodes available but scheduler isn't binding new pods.
alex: pasting a couple lines from scheduler.log I pulled from the leader:
```
I0308 12:34:21 scheduler admission: queue head pod/p-8a3 waiting; reason=nodeAffinityNotMatched
I0308 12:34:21 admission_controller: tokens_available=4
I0308 12:34:21 admission_loop: cannot advance queue, head unschedulable, returning early
I0308 12:34:22 scheduler: skipped 0 pods after head-of-queue block
```
this looks like the admission loop returns without scanning later entries.
taylor: that explains the skewed utilization — some pods behind could have relaxed affinity and would run, but they're stuck.
cheng: yeah this is classic head-of-line. suspect regression from the affinity short-circuit change last week (scheduler v2.7.1).
maria: can we identify the unschedulable pod(s) quickly?
alex: run this to list blockers: `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | grep Pending` then check `kubectl describe pod <name>` for nodeAffinity. Or use this JSONPath to list pending with nodeAffinity:
```
kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.status.phase=="Pending")]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity}{"\n"}{end}'
```

ops-bot: incident IR-342 created: "eu-west scheduler queue saturation", paging @sre-oncall
sre-oncall: on it. I'll do a controlled restart of the scheduler leader in eu-west to see if leadership handoff helps while we debug. ETA 5m.
taylor: careful—restart might temporarily increase scheduling latency; but I'm +1 if it unblocks. Also want to limit cost blowup: queued requests holding GPU tokens still count toward reserved throughput. ops, can we throttle ingress for non-critical tenants?
cheng: short term mitigation options:
1) identify pods with strict nodeAffinity and either relax or evict them (manual patch).
2) restart scheduler leader (sre-oncall).
3) patch scheduler to skip over unschedulable head entries (code change) — I have a minimal PR started.
alex: dropping the quick PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler/pulls/812 (WIP) — it adds a small loop to mark head as temporarily skippable when unschedulable for X seconds.
maria: for immediate unblock I'll patch one offending pod to remove the hard nodeAffinity and redeploy. Doing namespace serving/pods p-8a3 -> patch now.
cheng: great. postmortem action items: add e2e test for queue head skipping, telemetry for queue scan depth, and a backpressure metric that counts idle GPU vs queued requests. Also add runbook step to identify/evict affinity-blockers.
sre-oncall: scheduler restart done, leader switched, logs show admission loop resumed scanning. queue drained from 610 -> 34 in ~80s.
ops-bot: update: autoscaler no-op; capacity unchanged. cost impact: 1.2 GPU-hours wasted during saturation window (est).
taylor: thanks — will capture cost in the incident. assign follow-ups: cheng (patch & tests), alex (PR review), maria (exact pod list + cleanup), sre-oncall (post-restart monitor).
maria: ack. I pushed the temporary patch to the 3 pods causing the head blocks.
cheng: filing postmortem, will include timeline and fixes. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
alex: adding a small unit test to reproduce the unschedulable-head scenario in CI.
sre-oncall: monitoring eu-west 10m post-restart, all green so far.
maria: closing the incident ticket after we confirm metrics stable for 30m.
cheng: ping me if anything reappears, otherwise I'll merge the small skip patch after CI."
